title: Fluorine-free CO 2  electrolyzer for multicarbon products
content: Renewably powered CO2 electrolysis to multicarbon (C2+) products, including ethanol, offers a route to electrify chemical production, yet high-rate operation relies on fluorinated materials, particularly per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). These materials enable water, ion, and gas management required for efficient ethanol production but persist in the environment, prompting regulations that restrict their use. Attempts to replace PFAS in ionomers and gas diffusion layers (GDLs) have yielded only partial advances, with most candidates facing trade-offs among conductivity, hydrophobicity and chemical durability that limits C2+ production and stability. We thus sought PFAS-free alternatives for each component, beginning with the ionomer, where replacements are challenging due to its role in coordinating CO2, water, and ion transport. To address these requirements, we develop fluorine-free ionic polymer brushes on copper catalysts to decouple these functions. We also fabricate a silicon-polymer-coated GDL that enables 450 hours of stable CO2 reduction operation. Integrating this GDL with the ionic polymer brushes and a sulfonated polyether ether ketone membrane, we demonstrate a fully PFAS-free CO2 electrolyzer for C2+ production, achieving 43% ethanol faradaic efficiency in acidic conditions.
